results.project_title: Gamma oscillations as a prognostic marker for ketamine therapy in treatment resistant depression
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative
The typical selection method of therapies for patients with major depressive disorder has not changed for many
decades, involving a trial-and-error approach without firm biological rationale. This project examines a
candidate EEG biomarker to improve understanding of brain function with the long-term goal of optimally
selecting depressed patients for novel interventions such as ketamine/esketamine.

results.project_title: 2/2 A brief automated neurocognitive training to enhance the real-world impact of ketamine's rapid antidepressant effect
results.phr_text:
Project Narrative
 This project seeks to test the effectiveness and feasibility of delivering a brief digital intervention, designed to
rehabilitate self-worth through classical conditioning exercises, as an adjunct to intravenous ketamine treatments delivered
by embedded providers in real-world ketamine clinics. Ketamine, a fast-acting antidepressant, may rapidly prime the brain
for helpful forms of learning, and we seek to deliver such learning efficiently, through portable, low-cost, digital
techniques. This work could ultimately lead to the ability to treat depression more efficiently and effectively.

results.project_title: Ketamine for Treatment Resistant Late-Life Depression
results.phr_text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:    
   
Project Narrative:  Faced with an aging demographic profile towards a higher proportion of elderly Veterans, evidence- based, effective, safe, and efficient interventions for Veterans with late-life treatment resistant depression are critically needed. If optimal ketamine dose is identified and its antidepressant efficacy, safety, and tolerability, are affirmed in this randomizd controlled trial, there is genuine potential for a transformative impact on clinical practice.

results.project_title: NMDA receptor modulation for hyperarousal in PTSD
results.phr_text:
PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE:
Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a serious problem, with psychosocial impairment and
increased mortality from suicide. Further, it increases severity of affective and substance-use
disorders, and increases their mortality; yet there is no treatment that addresses interactions of
PTSD with other illnesses or its effects on suicidality. We will investigate effects of a medication
that addresses these problems on brain function and clinical symptoms in individuals with
severe PTSD and exaggerated physiological markers of anxiety.
